final_candidates.decision_summary: Charge-flipping substitution in the HA2 stem region with potential to form a new stabilizing salt bridge while preserving overall fold. Conservative physicochemical logic supports modest stability gain with low functional risk.
Very conservative hydrophobic substitution in the stem core; isoleucine may improve packing. Small but low-risk expected stability improvement.
Histidine can introduce pH-tolerant hydrogen bonding near the HA1 fusion peptide region. Moderate confidence due to some risk of perturbing local structure.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only condition with conservative candidate pool already settled; additional rounds without evidence would not improve ranking confidence.

history.rationale: HA2 stem residue (HA2 74) near the trimer interface; E-to-K can form compensating salt-bridge/hydrogen-bond networks with neighboring acidic residues, strengthening the stem coiled coil without touching the fusion peptide. Stem mutations here often raise thermostability while leaving head antigenicity intact.
Charge-optimizing surface substitution in HA2 stem region; conservative change with plausible stabilizing salt-bridge potential. Retain as lead pending further self-review.

Buried HA2 (≈HA2 102) position in the long stem helix at the trimer interface. An isoleucine substitution improves hydrophobic core packing and reduces cavity volume, which typically increases trimer stability and environmental persistence.
Very conservative hydrophobic substitution; beta-branched isoleucine may pack slightly better in the stem core. Modest but low-risk stability gain.

Aromatic head residue in the structurally conserved region near the C97-C139 disulfide cluster. Histidine can retain an aromatic stacking interaction while adding a hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor, modestly improving local fold rigidity.
His can form pH-dependent stabilizing interactions near the fusion peptide region, but risk of functional perturbation keeps confidence moderate.

Surface-exposed head residue adjacent to the conserved disulfide C305-C? region; the conservative extension to glutamate preserves the negative charge while allowing an additional stabilizing interaction with neighboring side chains.
Conservative lengthening of a surface acidic side chain; marginal stability effect expected, retained as backup.

Position in the 250s receptor-proximal scaffold; a conservative isoleucine-to-valine change can relieve local steric strain in the hydrophobic core while retaining packing, a small but favorable stability effect.
Very conservative hydrophobic core-adjacent change; small stabilization possible, low functional risk.

Exposed head residue; introducing lysine can add stabilizing surface electrostatics and reduce aggregation-prone neutral patches, improving persistence without perturbing the receptor-binding site or buried core.
Position 81 is within a glycosylation-adjacent epitope region of HA1; charge introduction near N-linked glycan sequons risks folding/trafficking disruption.

rejection.reason: Position 81 is within a glycosylation-adjacent epitope region of HA1; charge introduction near N-linked glycan sequons risks folding/trafficking disruption.
